question.prompt:
In quadrilateral \(ABCD,\) \(AB = 5,\) \(BC = 17,\) \(CD = 5,\) \(DA = 9,\) and \(BD\) is an integer. What is \(BD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_12A_Q10_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The diagonal \(BD\) is a side of both \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle BCD\), so its length must satisfy the triangle inequalities in both triangles. A triangle's third side is strictly between the difference and the sum of its other two sides.

Let \(x=BD\). From \(\triangle ABD\),
\[
9-5<x<9+5,
\qquad 4<x<14.
\]
From \(\triangle BCD\),
\[
17-5<x<17+5,
\qquad 12<x<22.
\]
Both restrictions hold exactly when \(12<x<14\). The endpoints are excluded because equality would make a triangle degenerate. The only integer in this range is \(13\), and it satisfies both triangles' strict inequalities. Therefore \(BD=13\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Apply the triangle inequalities
